summary: HOW'S EARTH🌍? is a simple web app that lets people check how temperatures have changed in Kochi, Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai. It gets monthly temperature data (T2M) from the NASA POWER API for 2001-2025 and turns it into yearly averages. It draws a graph with a trend line and uses linear regression to find the rate of change and a p-value, so users can see if a trend is strong or could be chance. It explains the result in plain English and can compare two cities. It makes climate data easy to explore for people with no science background, and it is honest about its limits.
details:
What it does: The user picks a city and clicks one button. The app gets NASA POWER monthly temperature data, turns the 12 months of each year into one average, and draws a graph with a trend line. It reports the rate of change, total change, p-value and whether the trend is statistically significant. A "SO, HOW'S EARTH?" section explains it simply. Users can also compare two cities on one graph.

How it works: Python code calls the NASA POWER monthly API for the city's coordinates. It ignores missing values and uses only years with all 12 months. SciPy fits the trend line. Simple if/else rules write the explanation.

Benefits and impact: It helps ordinary people explore real NASA data and see the difference between a real trend and random ups and downs.

*Tools:* Python, Streamlit, Pandas, Matplotlib, Requests, SciPy, GitHub.

Creative and careful choices: The app treats Earth as a friend whose temperature we check. It uses no fake data, shows friendly errors, and states clearly that one city's trend cannot prove the cause of climate change. NASA POWER temperatures come from a model (MERRA-2) over map squares, and the app says so.
